Commentary.Commentary: With Afghanistan playing a pacer it will be interesting to see how much will they use him and do they start with him first up.
So 342 is what Afghanistan have got. Their total is not far away from the average first innings total of around 370 on this venue. Join us in a short while for Bangladesh's reply.

As for Bangladesh's bowling, they were subpar at times on Day 1 but it was a better showing from them this morning. The cameo from Rashid Khan hurt them but they managed to get 5 wickets for just 71 runs. Taijul Islam was the star with the ball picking up 4 wickets. Nayeem Hasan and skipper, Shakib Al Hasan were good with the ball too picking up 2 wickets apiece. Mehidy Hasan and Mahmudullah too got into the wickets column with one each.

Asghar Afghan and Afsar Zazai though could not continue their good work from Day 1 and the experienced Afghan departed just 8 runs shy of his 100. Afghanistan kept losing wickets at regular intervals and it looked like they would struggle to get to 330 but a terrific, quickfire 50 from their skipper, Rashid Khan took them close to 350.

After winning the toss, Rashid Khan opted to bat first. It looked like the visitors would struggle against the quality spin of Bangladesh losing 3 wickets under 80 but then we witnessed a historic innings. Rahmat Shah and Asghar Afghan steadied the ship and put together a 120-run stand. In the process, Rahmat became the first Afghanistan player to get to the triple figure mark in Test cricket. He though could not continue his good work and departed straightaway after reaching the milestone. Nabi followed him without troubling the scorers. It looked like Afghanistan would collapse but a brilliant 81-run stand put the visitors back on top.
A brilliant quickfire fifty from the Afghanistan skipper has taken his side over 340. A total that is a not just competitive but also very good on this wicket.

On the weather, Tino says it was dark yesterday but today it is starting to brighten up. Mawoyo feels if Afghanistan can score 400 then they would put themselves in command.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of Day 2 of this one-off Test between Bangladesh and Afghanistan. After a historic Day 1 for Afghanistan, the hosts would look to put on a better show today. The ploy to not play any genuine pacer seems to have backfired for Bangladesh as on the first day of this Test they looked one dimensional at times. Afghanistan, on the other hand, will hope that the  experienced Asghar Afghan can continue his good work along with Afsar Zazai and build on their stand. Another record is on the cards for the visitors as their former skipper who is unbeaten on 88 is inching closer to becoming their second player to score a ton. Will Afghanistan continue to prove why they belong with the big boys or will the sun shine brighter on the Bangla shores?
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Bangladesh's aim tomorrow will be to bundle the visitors out as quickly as possible as they know they will have to bat 4th here and they would not want to be staring down a big first innings score. Afghanistan, on the other hand, will want to keep batting and add as many more runs as possible. One believes 350 should be a good total. Join us for what could be another absorbing day of Test cricket. Day 2 begins at 1000 local (0400 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

The Bangladesh side filled their XI with only spinners but the wicket did not play on Day 1 as they thought it would have. There was not a lot of turn and bounce. It was hard work for their bowlers. Islam was the pick though as he took a 2-fer. Nayeem Hasan was also good. Mehidy and Shakib though were a touch disappointing.

Rahmat raked up the first ever Test ton for Afghanistan while Afghan got to his half century and he is still unbeaten. Just as it seemed that Bangladesh were looking to crawl back into the game through 2 quick wickets, Afghan, along with Afsar Zazai have added 74 unbeaten runs and have made sure the visitors head into Day 2 on top.

Afghanistan's start though was not up to the mark as the openers, after a fighting first hour of the first session, went back to the pavilion in quick time. Shahidi too did not stay out for long. Rahmat Shah though combined with Asghar Afghan to add 120 runs and take the visitors to a commanding position. The two played with a lot of determination and were also not bogged down as they played attacking shots on timely occasions too.

Tremendous day of Test cricket where the Afghans end with the upper hand. They have justified the decision of their skipper of batting first and they will be very happy with how things have ended on Day 1.

Afghanistan have done better than the last time they played a Test in the subcontinent. But the lack of experience has been quite evident. They started off cautiously but have been unable to build on the budding stands. Rahmat Shah has shown technique and composure but he needs someone to hang around with him if Afghanistan are to reach a decent total.

LUNCH! Bangladesh will be the side heading into the break with their heads held high. They have done brilliantly to peg the visitors back. In a side where all the front line bowlers are spinners, without any surprise all wickets have fallen to the spinners. Taijul Islam has been the pick of the bowlers in the morning session, picking up two wickets and in the process becoming the second highest wicket-taker for Bangladesh in Tests. Mahmudullah was the other bowler to get into the wickets column.

Shahidi looks to play it late but the ball skids through, flies off the outside edge and Sarkar at first slip takes it nicely. The Bangladesh players are ecstatic. We are all set for the game to begin. Ihsanullah and Ibrahim Zadran stride out to open the innings for Afghanistan. Taijul Islam to start the proceedings with the new ball for Bangladesh.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is down with the pitch report. He says there is a bit of grass but nothing the seamers can take anything off. Informs that it is a dry surface and there will be a bit of bounce off the surface. Mawayo feels the captain winning the toss would bat first.

Bangladesh skipper, Shakib says that he was looking to bat first as well. Tells the boys are up for the challenge and know that Afghanistan will be tough team to beat. Informs that they are going with all 4 spinners.

Afghanistan skipper, Rashid Khan says that the wicket looks good to bat on and hence he is batting first. Tells it is a proud moment for him to lead the side at such a young age and he hopes to do well. Seconds the thought that Bangladesh have a good record at home but they have done well in their prepartaion and now they just have to give their best.

TOSS - We are all set for the flip of coin. Bangladesh skipper, Shakib Al Hasan has the coin in hand. Up it goes and lands in favour of the visitors. AFGHANISTAN OPT TO BAT!

Bangladesh and Afghanistan, the two spin-heavy sides collide against each other at Chittagong in One-off Test before they get into the white ball mode for the tri-series involving Zimbabwe. Bangladesh's last Test encounter was against the Kiwis in New Zealand before the World Cup which they lost. However, at home, Bangladesh are a powerful Test team and Afghanistan, playing only the third Test will be vary of that. Shakib Al Hasan is back to lead the Test side. He had a terrific World Cup on a personal note and would look to continue doing the same for his side in the longest format of the game. The Afghans raked up a win against Ireland in their second Test and would like to repeat the same against the hosts to take their rivalry to another level. They will look at their skipper Rashid Khan for all the inspiration along with their batters like Rahmat Shah and Hashmatullah Shahidi to tackle the Bangladeshi spin threat.  Notably, this game is not a part of ICC World Test Championship but Bangladesh who are part of the tournament will look to have a positive start before getting into the grove of the 2-year long tournament. In all, we are in for an exciting Test match. Welcome to our coverage.
